text:
noor: Quick postmortem from today's aurora-lite-int4 onboard run. We observed 0.33% funcall schema failures tied to truncated param values for `annotate_doc` around 11:07 UTC.
jack: Can you paste some raw samples?
noor: Copied three from the staging logs:
```
{"tool":"annotate_doc","params":{"doc_id":123,"note":"Needs review: missing figure references"}}
{"tool":"annotate_doc","params":{"doc_id":123,"note":"Needs review: missing figure referen"}}
{"tool":"annotate_doc","params":{"doc_id":123}}
```
meera: Looks like a tail-truncation of the `note` field, sometimes dropping entirely. Likely correlated with streaming chunk boundaries + int4 tail-kludge.
jack: Did mirror fp32 path show same behavior?
noor: Mirror fp32 was clean. Float path keep `note` in 99.99% of samples. Only int4 streaming had the 0.33% drop.
meera: Proposed mitigations: add `schema_lint: permissive` on the route to accept field-order variants and coerce missing optional fields, but for required fields we must enforce. Add `repair.path: suffix_restore_v1` that attempts a single constrained 1-token-infill if `note` is short and original prompt mandated its presence.
jack: We should gate repairs by tool: `repair_allowed: [annotate_doc]` only for low-risk ops. Also add `repair_audit` telemetry tag for every repaired response.
noor: I ran a small harness where we injected synthetic boundary splits. Suffix_restore recovered ~78% of missing-note cases and reduced consumer errors from 0.33% -> 0.08%. Median latency for repaired requests rose by ~18ms.
meera: Important: add a semantic-checker to avoid hallucinated fills. Remediation only allowed if the recovered text overlaps with existing tokens from earlier chunks or matches a short regex pattern present in the prompt.
jack: Ops plan:
- enable `schema_lint: permissive` and `repair_allowed` for canary only
- expose telemetry: `funcall.schema_status` and `funcall.parse_reason` with enums: missing_key,truncation,malformed_json,order_only
- run 150k sample harness across float/int4/mirror and collect `repair_precision` and `false_repair_rate`
- rollback quick threshold: false_repair_rate > 0.02% or user-impact > 0.1%
noor: I'll prepare the canary config and a small PR for the runtime change. Meera can own the harness tests. Jack will update the rollout dashboard to separate runtime vs schema success.
meera: I'll also add an eval that forces repairs and compares repaired text against ground truth to compute precision.
test-bot: canary scheduled: aurora-lite-int4 annotate_doc repair opt-in on staging at 2026-03-26T09:30Z.
noor: Thanks everyone. I'll post the 24h telemetry snapshot once the canary completes.
